IDIOM MEANING EXAMPLE GET ON THE BANDWAGON To join an activity that has become very popular. The success of the product led many firms to try to get on the bandwagon. KEEP THE CHIN UP To be stalwart and courageous in a tough situation. Don't let the difficulties intimidate you; keep your chin up. WALK OUT ON To suddenly leave a job, a relationship or other situation. Everyone was shocked when he walked out on his wife of fourteen years. COME OUT SWINGING To be confrontational. He came out swinging at his critics, accusing them of having their own agenda. BEEF UP To become big and muscular. We need to find some new players to beef up the team. TURN ASIDE To refuse entry to somewhere. His job application was turned aside when they saw his criminal record. TIDE OVER Temporary help (often financial) Have another piece of cake. It'll tide you over till supper. CRACK UP Go through an emotional breakdown. The entire group cracked up at the joke of their teacher.

Everyday communication uses what we know as phrasal verbs to express ideas easily and make them sound more native-like.

slides.title: To Consider 1. Verb + Preposition combination receive the stress on the verb particle. E.G. We need to look after the babies. 2. Verb + Adverb combination receives the stress on the adverb particle. E.G. The thieves just ran away. 3. Verb + Adverb + Preposition combination receives the stress on the adverb particle. E.G. The family is bearing up under the trials. 4. Some phrasal verbs may be separable. That is to say, the object goes in the middle of the particles. This mainly happens when the object is a pronoun. E.G. We need to call it off. 5. Separable phrasal verbs work also together. E.G. We called off the meeting.

Functional English

slides.title: We use phrasal verbs to sound more natural and shorten phrases when communicating.
visibleTexts: We use phrasal verbs to sound more natural and shorten phrases when communicating.
Function Examples Express actions in a more natural way. I need to look for a new nanny. You have turned down the offer they made us. We needed to catch up with the girls.
To consider Phrasal verbs may be used in any context, that’s what makes them common and a natural way of communication.

Knock it off! Have you ever met someone who is so annoying that you can not stand him? I think we all have. Coming across with such a character and having him around may make us shout at some point ‘hey man, knock it off! However, being in peace with everyone is something we all must go for. We need to bear in mind that each person is different so that brings up different situations to deal with. Nevertheless, neither disrespect nor abuse should be born from anyone, so we need to set limits and boundaries.
